content: Discuss the results of your blood sugar monitoring with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. This medication may increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your exposure to the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen while wearing protective clothing when outdoors. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary. It may reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby, and tipranavir could be part of that treatment. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can affect the removal of tipranavir from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include apalutamide, macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), and rifampin. Tipranavir, when combined with ritonavir, can either accelerate or slow the removal of other drugs from your body, affecting their function. Aspirin may increase the risk of bleeding when used with this medication. However, if your doctor has advised you to take low-dose aspirin (81-162 milligrams daily) to prevent heart attack or stroke, continue taking it unless instructed otherwise. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Consult your doctor or pharmacist about using reliable backup birth control methods while on this medication. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms like unconsciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular lab and medical tests (e.g., liver function, HIV RNA levels, blood sugar, blood counts, cholesterol, and triglyceride levels) are necessary. Attend all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store unopened bottles in the refrigerator. After opening, capsules may be stored at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Once opened, this medication expires after 60 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
